Committee: Education Policy
Sponsor: Fincher
Analyst: Daniel Davenport
Date: 04/05/2021
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 440 as introduced could decrease federal funds received by the State Department of Education (SDE) and the local boards of education, cumulatively, by an estimated $500 million annually, according to SDE, due to the prohibition of the use of assessments aligned with national standards, as provided by this bill. Currently public school students are administered the National Assessment of Education Progress (NAEP), which could be prohibited by this bill, but which participation is required to be eligible to receive certain federal funds.
Terri Collins, Chair
Education Policy

Committee: Judiciary
Sponsor: England
Analyst: Pete Grogan
Date: 02/02/2021
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 107 as introduced repeals the Habitual Felony Offender Act and removes references to this act in the Code of Alabama 1975. This bill also provides for any defendant currently in the custody of the Department of Corrections or under the supervision of the Board of Pardons and Paroles or the courts for an offense that he or she was sentenced pursuant to the Habitual Felony Offender Act to be resentenced pursuant to the sentencing standards in place at the time of resentencing.
This bill would 1) decrease the obligations of the Department of Corrections by an undetermined amount dependent upon the number of inmates that receive a reduced sentence; 2) increase the obligations of the Board of Pardons and Paroles by an undetermined amount dependent upon the number of inmates that receive a reduced sentence and are eligible for parole or mandatory release; and 3) increase the obligations of the circuit courts by an undetermined amount dependent upon the number of resentencing hearings held.
Jim Hill, Chair
Judiciary

Committee: State Government
Sponsor: Clarke
Analyst: John Friedenreich
Date: 02/24/2021
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 179 as amended and reported by the Committee on State Government will allow the Director of the State Port Authority to appoint and fix the salaries of two additional non-merit system executive level employees who could replace current merit system executive level employees who retire or otherwise leave the employment of the port authority. This could increase the Port Authority's obligations by an unknown amount that would be dependent upon the salaries established for the two non-merit executive level employees and whether they are additional employees or replacement for existing employees, as well as the salaries of the merit system employee being replaced, if applicable. The average salary of the nine executive level employees authorized prior to this bill is approximately $157,000.
Chris Pringle, Chair
State Government
